survey: A wooden barrel stands upright on a plank deck, seen from slightly above and in front. The body is made of vertical staves that bulge evenly at the middle and narrow toward the top and bottom. Four dark iron hoops wrap the body: one at the top, one at the upper belly, one at the lower belly and one at the bottom. Each hoop follows the curve of the staves and sits snug against them. The stave seams line up across the hoops. The top head is a disc of diagonal planks with a raised rim, visible as an ellipse. The barrel's bottom rests flat on the deck and casts a contact shadow, so it is supported. The scratches on the hoops and the drip on one stave are surface wear, not structural problems. The hoop count is normal for a barrel, and there are no invented parts.

errors.what: The head looks like a separate lid laid on top of the barrel: a disc with its own raised rim that sits on the stave ends. On a real barrel the head is set into a groove just below the top of the staves, so the stave ends rise slightly above it. As drawn, the head does not look held in place by the staves.

fix: Set the barrel's top head into the barrel: a flat wooden disc slightly below the top edge of the staves, with the stave ends forming a thin raised rim around it. Do not draw a separate lid sitting on top.
